protocol.name: treeland_activation_token_unstable_v1

protocol.description:
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development. It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways, without incrementing the interface major version and without prior notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or semantics remaining stable across releases.
This protocol lets a single privileged client, the DDE application manager, obtain an xdg-activation-v1 token for an application it is about to launch. The compositor only checks that the caller is that privileged client; deciding whether an application may be activated is the client's responsibility.
A token obtained through this protocol is accepted by xdg_activation_v1.activate() from any client and always results in a real activation: it is never downgraded to an attention request, even though it carries no serial and no originating surface.
The compositor must reject bind attempts from non-privileged clients.
The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

interface.name: treeland_activation_token_manager_v1
interface.description: A global that mints xdg-activation-v1 tokens on behalf of a privileged DDE client. Binding it is restricted: the compositor must reject bind attempts from non-privileged clients.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the treeland_activation_token_manager_v1 object. Tokens already delivered through this manager are not affected.

request.name: request_token

description.summary: create a new activation token object

request.description: Create a treeland_activation_token_v1 object for the application identified by app_id. The compositor mints the token and delivers it with the token event on the new object. app_id is advisory: the compositor does not use it for any policy decision, only for logging and tracing.

arg.name: app_id
arg.summary: advisory app id of the application that will be activated

interface.name: treeland_activation_token_v1
interface.description:
A token object delivers exactly one token event and is then inert. The token stays valid for a limited time and is consumed by the first xdg_activation_v1.activate() request that uses it.
The client must destroy the object after receiving the token.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the treeland_activation_token_v1 object. This does not invalidate a token that was already delivered.

event.name: token
event.description: Sent once, in response to the request_token request that created this object. The event is delivered as part of that request's dispatch, so the client must add its listener before the next wl_display_dispatch()/roundtrip().
